trip_pattern: Depart Friday, return Sunday (2-night weekend trip) — NOT Saturday-to-Sunday. weekend_span_days is only used for the calendar-availability check; kids-custody weekends are all-or-nothing across Thu evening-Sun, so no separate Friday availability check is needed. Thursday evening is an acceptable alternative departure Trevor would consider, but Friday is the automated default.
deal_definition: Round-trip fare that is at least deal_threshold_pct below the best available historical baseline for that specific route in price_history.json (prefer the median of self-logged 'observations' once 3+ exist, otherwise the seeded 'seeded_typical_price_range' low end). Routes with no price_history.json entry fall back to explicit deal-site language (e.g. 'X% off', 'price drop', 'error fare') as a secondary signal — a generic low-looking price with no such framing does not qualify.
route_weekend_check_scope: full — check every (route, weekend) pair every day, no rotation/cap. Accepted trade-off: this is a much higher volume of automated requests to Google Flights than a conservative rotation, with real (unquantified) risk of tripping Google's own anti-abuse rate-limiting. Prioritized anyway because flight pricing is dynamic and near-real-time freshness matters more here than minimizing that risk.
price_check_tool: fast-flights (PyPI package, no API key, no official rate-limit contract — be as polite a caller as full daily coverage allows: pace requests, don't hammer retries on errors)
email_send_method: Gmail REST API over HTTPS (gmail.googleapis.com), authenticated via OAuth refresh token scoped only to gmail.send for tkfred02ram@gmail.com. Uses GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN env vars (see AGENT_PROMPT.md step 8b). Chosen over SMTP because this sandbox's network policy blocks port 587 entirely; chosen over third-party ESPs (Resend/SendGrid/Brevo) because they require an owned+authenticated domain to deliver reliably to Gmail/Yahoo/Microsoft, which this account doesn't have. The Gmail MCP connector has no send capability at all, only draft creation.
gmail_oauth_reminder_note: The OAuth consent screen is in Google's 'Testing' publishing status (unverified app), so refresh tokens expire exactly 7 days after issuance — no way around this short of buying a domain and completing Google's full app verification, which Trevor opted not to do. See AGENT_PROMPT.md step 1b for the proactive reminder-email logic that warns before each expiry. When Trevor re-authorizes (re-running the local OAuth flow and updating GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN in the cloud environment), update gmail_oauth_issued_at to that day's date.
gmail_send_method_status_note: As of 2026-10-15: the raw GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN env-var flow described in AGENT_PROMPT.md step 8b is confirmed dead (token exchange returns invalid_grant) and has been since shortly after gmail_oauth_issued_at (2026-08-24) + 7 days; it was never re-issued/updated. Daily runs since at least 2026-10-12 have instead sent deal-alert emails successfully via the Gmail MCP connector's send_message tool (mcp__Gmail__send_message, supports htmlBody), which contradicts AGENT_PROMPT.md's claim that the Gmail MCP connector has no send capability — that claim is stale; the connector gained send ability at some point and recent runs use it. Recommend treating mcp__Gmail__send_message as the current primary send path and not alerting Trevor on gmail_oauth_issued_at staleness unless mcp__Gmail__send_message itself starts failing.
observation_baseline_quality_note: Found 2026-10-21: for a handful of thin/remote routes (seen so far: HOU-CZM, HOU-FCA), the daily fast-flights observation series for a given exact (depart_date, return_date) pair is bimodal — it alternates between a low cluster (e.g. ~$650-700) and a much higher cluster (e.g. ~$2900-5000), often with the exact same price repeated for 4-6 consecutive days before jumping to the other cluster. This looks like a scraper artifact (inconsistent itinerary/connection selection by fast-flights for low-frequency routes) rather than real fare volatility, and it drags the per-pair observation median far above the seeded_typical_price_range, producing false 'exceptional deal' readings (e.g. HOU-CZM 2026-12-11/13 showed 76.9% off, HOU-FCA 2027-01-01/03 showed 63.8% off, both withheld from the 2026-10-21 email). Mitigation applied that day: before emailing, cross-check each candidate deal's price against the route's seeded_typical_price_range — if price is not actually below the seeded low end (not just the polluted observation median), and/or the observation series for that exact pair shows long (4+) runs of exact-duplicate prices spanning a >2x range, treat it as a likely data-quality artifact and withhold it from the email (but still log the observation and do NOT add it to seen_deals.json, so it can be re-evaluated once the series stabilizes). This heuristic is not in AGENT_PROMPT.md's literal algorithm — it is a conservative judgment call per the 'be conservative about what counts as a qualifying deal' guidance, applied the same way the Aug 12 2026 cross-weekend-pooling false-deal incident was handled. Future runs should keep applying this sanity check and can update this note if more routes exhibit the pattern or if a cleaner fix is found.
